backstory:
Ravi is a 34-year-old male working as a High school chemistry teacher. For about 1.5 years, they have been dealing with anxiety symptoms (undiagnosed).
Deep down they believe: "If I can't keep it together in front of my students, I shouldn't be trusted to guide them."
When things get hard, this is the thought that comes: "I can't believe I lost control like that; what if they think I'm not capable?"
How the self-stigma usually shows up: still catches himself thinking he should be able to handle a classroom without issue, but has started to counter that thought -- recognizes that many effective teachers experience similar challenges, and that his anxiety doesn't define his ability to teach or be a good father, even if the doubt still catches him on a bad day and takes a moment to answer rather than being gone for good. Some weeks the answer comes easily; other weeks it takes him most of the drive home to talk himself back down, and he still isn't sure which version of the week he'll get.
